title: finding(app-shell): three BLOCK_CONFIG blocks resolve to no runtime-judgeable schema on either face — the exemption bucket objectui#8216 gate must carry
body:
Found by the census objectui#8216 asked for (branch `claude/issue-8216-block-config-schema-parity`). Filed unassigned. This card owns the EXEMPTION rows objectui#8216's gate lands with: each of the three blocks below is exempt there with a reason and this card's number, and each exemption is self-deleting — it goes red the moment its block resolves to a schema on either face.

Measured on `origin/main` `f20e57d62`, installed `@objectstack/spec` `17.2.0`.

## The census result

22 `BLOCK_CONFIG` entries. Each block was resolved against two faces:

- `ComponentPropsMap[type]` from `@objectstack/spec/ui` — 42 rows, strict objects that refuse an undeclared key by name;
- the `@object-ui/types/zod` node registry, derived mechanically by reading the `type` literal off every exported Zod object — 104 rows, `BaseSchema.passthrough()` so an undeclared key is KEPT rather than refused.

18 blocks resolve to a spec props shape, 4 to a node schema (`object-grid`, `object-form`, `object-kanban` on both, `grid` on the node face only), and **3 resolve to neither**:

| block | in ComponentPropsMap | in the zod node registry | in PageComponentType | in BLOCK_TYPE_META |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `element:definition-list` | no | no | no | yes |
| `element:repeater` | no | no | no | yes |
| `ai:input` | no | no | no | no |

## Why the gap is real and not a naming accident

All three have working, registered renderers reached through `ComponentRegistry`, and two of them are offered in the palette. What none of them has is a DECLARED key set that anything can judge an authored document against:

- `element:definition-list` and `element:repeater` are registered in `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/data-list.tsx` with a registry `inputs` list — a different face, on a different table, judged by a different gate (`apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`, objectui#8067 / objectui#8068). That face declares TOP-LEVEL inputs only; the nested item shape of `definition-list`'s `items` is described in an `inputs` DESCRIPTION string, in prose.
- `ai:input` has no renderer at all beyond the opt-in placeholder list, and no palette entry — that one is its own card, filed separately.

The measured cost of the absence is not hypothetical: reading the `definition-list` renderer by hand turned up a live spelling mismatch its designer controls have carried all along, filed separately. A gate cannot find that class here, because there is nothing for it to read.

## The decision this needs

Whether objectui-native page blocks (blocks that are in the palette but not in `PageComponentType`) should carry a declared key set at all, and on which face:

- **A — a `@object-ui/types` zod node schema per block.** Puts them on the same face `object-grid` / `object-form` / `object-kanban` / `grid` already use, so one gate covers all of `BLOCK_CONFIG`. The face is `passthrough()`, so it declares rather than refuses; objectui#5155 is the standing argument about that.
- **B — upstream them into `PageComponentType` and `ComponentPropsMap`.** Gets a STRICT oracle and one vocabulary, at the cost of a spec change per block and of committing objectstack to blocks it does not model today.
- **C — declare the nested item shapes on the registry `inputs` face** and let objectui#8071's per-member pin work cover them. Smallest change; leaves the designer table judged by a gate that reads `inputs` rather than a schema.
- **D — leave them undeclared, ledgered here.** The honest null option: three blocks, two of them low-traffic, in a startup-stage repo that does not expand declaration surface without pull.

⚠️ Grading is triage's. What this card asks for is that the three exemptions in objectui#8216's gate stop being permanent by default — an exemption with no owning decision is the hiding place the ratchet idiom exists to prevent.

## Related

objectui#8216 (the gate that carries the exemptions) · objectui#8067 / objectui#8068 / objectui#8071 (the registry `inputs` face and its per-member pins) · objectui#5155 (BaseSchema openness) · the two sibling cards filed from the same census, on `element:definition-list`'s item spelling and on `ai:input`'s orphan panel
